long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in a large working-class family in Paris, Gérard Perse left school at fifteen and first worked beside his father, a house painter. He moved into produce trading, opened grocery stores and developed a profitable supermarket group. That self-built retail success gave him the means to pursue a long-standing fascination with Saint-Émilion wine.

Perse bought Château Monbousquet in 1993, followed by Pavie-Decesse, Château Pavie and other Bordeaux properties. He overhauled vineyard practices and cellars, assembling specialists around a concentrated, exacting style that divided critics but elevated the estates’ standing. Château Pavie reached Saint-Émilion’s Premier Grand Cru Classé A rank in 2012. He also expanded into hospitality around the village before his death at 75.
